messages:
raj: Observing new p99 spikes (~2.8s -> 4.5s) after yesterday's kernel selector change + enabling cross-region fallback. metric alert fired at ~13:42 UTC. Anyone else seeing correlated KV miss amplification?

lina: Yep saw the alert. Initial read: more KV misses on eu-west->us-west fallback traces. p50/p95 stable, tail is the problem.

sam: I pulled a sample trace: 
```
TRACE ID: 0x7f2a
kernel: matmul-v2
microbatch: 8
route: eu-west -> us-west (fallback)
kv_hits: 12
kv_misses: 47
latency_ms: 4500
stack: wait->kvcache-miss->cross-region-rpc->kernel-queue
```

chen: That kv_misses / microbatch ratio looks bad. When fallback happens we rehydrate prefix KV across region which increases RPCs and serialization overhead. Combined with matmul-v2 kernel's slightly higher setup time, it amplifies tail.

raj: Agreed. Two hypotheses: (1) cross-region fallback increases distributed KV miss amplification (many small RPCs), (2) new kernel selection increased per-microbatch setup so hits the slow path more often for big sequences.

lina: Quick experiment proposal: force local-region routing (no fallback) for a small % (5%) of traffic and compare p99. Also try reducing microbatch to 4 for the fallback path to see if smaller batches reduce amplification.

sam: I can roll the traffic split. Also we'll enable detailed kv telemetry for those buckets (kv.proto + rpc timings).

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: route-control/experiment-tail-2026 -> 5% holdout, target: eu-west region. Job id: rc-2026-44.

chen: For reference, current important config snippet: 
```
"routing": {
  "policy": "latency_preferred",
  "fallback": {
    "enabled": true,
    "max_hop_ms": 1200
  }
},
"microbatch": {
  "target_size": 8,
  "max_delay_ms": 10
}
```

raj: If fallback path adds ~30-60ms per KV RPC and we do 40 extra RPCs due to misses, that's a few seconds stacked with kernel setup. We should try: drop microbatch target to 4 on fallback, and increase local-pref threshold to avoid fallback unless region latency>600ms.

lina: Also adding a small prefix-cache on the serving node to absorb rehydration spikes could reduce RPCs for repeated keys during fallback. We saw similar pattern in last year's eu-fallback burst.

sam: Rolling config change in experiment: fallback microbatch_target=4, fallback_local_threshold=600ms for 5% canary. Will post results in ~15m.

deploy-bot: Config update applied to rc-2026-44. Plan: monitor p50/p95/p99 + kv_miss_rate + cross-region_rpcs.

raj: Thanks. If p99 drops back near baseline we can consider making it the default. If not, next steps: profile kernel setup path and trace serialization costs.

lina: Noting we should also check quantization path: matmul-v2 had slightly different memory layout which can increase first-token kernel setup. Might be compounding.

sam: Got first 10 minutes: p99 in canary bucket fell from 4.5s to 2.6s, kv_miss_rate down ~40%, cross-region_rpcs down ~55%. Promising.

chen: Nice. Can you capture a flamegraph for the slow traces before we change anything else? Need to be sure kernel setup vs RPC is majority.

sam: Will grab flamegraphs and attach to the ticket (TICKET-RT-887).

raj: Great. Plan after this: if canary holds, promote changes and open a follow-up to revisit kernel selector thresholds and add small local prefix cache for fallback flows.

lina: Add note: update rollout docs so on future kernel swaps we consider fallback amplification. :memo:

sam: ACK.

raj: Closing loop — will check again after 1hr and post final stats. :eyes:
